subject: Polaris dedicated migration: capacity tuning & cutover runbook
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris dedicated migration: capacity tuning & cutover runbook

Hi team,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Following up with a concise plan for the hosted->dedicated migration for Polaris (DEAL-78420). Goal here is to validate the sizing assumptions, run a small acceptance traffic test, and lock the final cutover window with a clear fallback.

Proposed pre-cutover checklist (high level):
- Confirm model QPS and 95th p50 token latency from hosted traces (output attached).
- Finalize target GPU pool: initial target = 12xA100-80GB (8 active, 4 standby).
- Validate batching profile and expected GPU utilization with synthetic replay (we should aim for sustained 60-75% GPU util).
- Run KV/prefix cache warmup script during acceptance window.
- Smoke test fallback to smaller quantized variant (q4_0) under load.
- Cutover window: 3 hours with 30m rollback hold and staged traffic ramping (10% / 40% / 100%).

I've attached a spreadsheet with the detailed capacity numbers (polaris_capacity_checklist.xlsx) and a draft runbook for fallback steps. Please review the sizing rows under the "validation" tab — the concurrency per model assumes 3.2 tokens/sec average and a 1.8x burst multiplier.

Action items: Marcus — can you run a quick calibration of expected GPU concurrency and confirm the 8/4 active/standby split?
Priyom — please confirm the quantized variant latency regressions and if there are any known decoding edge cases.
Emma / Polaris SRE — confirm a preferred cutover date range and any maintenance blackout windows.

I'll hold a short dry-run on July 27th to exercise the playback and KV warming; please flag conflicts.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — good draft. Quick notes after looking at the telemetry:
- The hosted traces for the last 30 days show median prompt length 62 tokens and median generation 24 tokens. 95th percentile latency is closer to our earlier estimate (1.6x the median under burst).
- With those numbers, our spreadsheet indicates 10 A100-80GB will comfortably hold the steady-state plus an 18% headroom; 12 keeps us safe for the first week while we monitor.
- Concurrency profile: target avg concurrency per GPU = ~45 streams (with continuous batching optimizations). We'll validate on the replay.

I ran a short synthetic run against a staging model and attached updated "model-variant-mapping.csv" with expected throughput deltas between fp16 and q4_0 variants. Noticed one customer prompt pattern that spikes tokenization cost; flagged in the sheet.

I'll schedule the calibration job for Jul 25 (replay + KV warmup). If the job confirms utilization numbers, I support 12xA100 with 4 standby.

Marcus

On Tue, Jul 17, 2028 at 11:02 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> [Marcus' message truncated]

Thanks — couple of technical caveats from the model-ops side:
- q4_0 performance: latency uplift for q4_0 versus fp16 is roughly +18-25% for generation-heavy prompts; for short-turn prompts the delta is smaller. We should pick the fallback model only for traffic segments where quality tolerance is acceptable.
- KV cache behavior: cold-started keys cause a transient 2-3x increase in token compute for the first 5k tokens per session. The warming script should be run against a longer tail of user prompts to avoid noisy spike during acceptance.

Proposed additions to the runbook:
1) Pre-cutover: run 45-minute progressive warmup (5m, 10m, 30m) with increasing QPS.
2) Acceptance: verify GPU p95 latency and end-to-end API success rate > 99.5% for 30 minutes at 40% traffic.
3) Rollback: immediate traffic switch back to hosted API (DNS/edge controlled) + telemetry tag to mark the failed cutover.

I've attached a small PDF snippet of the fallback play (cutover-fallback-runbook.pdf). Also, please add a short section on SLA exception requests we might need to surface to Polaris procurement if they expect tight latency SLAs.

Priyom
Staff ML Infra | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — Polaris SRE here. A few points from our side: 
- Maintenance windows: prefer weekdays 02:00-05:00 UTC (we can do Jul 29 or Aug 2).
- We require a standby rollback option that reverts traffic in <15 minutes for the first 48 hours post-cutover. Is the DNS+edge rollback path tested?
- Procurement note: our legal/procurement team wants the dedicated capacity commitment limited to 90 days with a 30-day notice to scale down. We will surface that in the DocuSign.

We'll run a dry-run on Jul 27 (02:30 UTC) — will that line up with your warmup? We can be available for the first 2 hours after cutover to validate downstream telemetry.

—Emma

- Capacity: provision 12xA100-80GB (8 active, 4 standby) for initial week. Procurement ask to limit the minimum commitment to 90 days noted — I'll mark this in HubSpot and route to Sales Ops.
- Attachments: polaris_capacity_checklist.xlsx, cutover-fallback-runbook.pdf, model-variant-mapping.csv. DocuSign link will be sent once procurement aligns on the 90-day clause.

I'll send a short invite for the dry-run and add a final checklist release the morning of Jul 29th. Thanks all — callout to SRE for the <15m rollback verification during the dry-run.
